newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp profits up but slow chip sales cast a shadow.
newsitem.headline: Sharp profits up but slow chip sales cast a shadow.

text.p: Japanese electronics maker Sharp Corp said on Monday it made a modest gain in its group profit for the half year to September, but a sluggish global chip market was still casting a shadow over its business.
Sharp announced a group net profit of 24.23 billion yen ($216 million) for the six months, the first half of this business year, up 8.9 percent from the same period last year.
A recent recovery in demand for its mainstay products such as liquid crystal display (LCD) panels and flash memory chips eased some of the pain from a weak global chip market.
Group sales grew 7.8 percent to 865.36 billion yen ($7.72 billion) from a year earlier, Sharp said.

"Recovering demand for liquid crystal display computer panels helped support the half-year net profit. The damage from lower chip market prices appears to be smaller than that for other companies," a Sharp spokesman said.
But he said a plunge in global chip prices earlier this year still clouded the company's business prospects for the full year to next March 31.

Sharp revised down its full-year group net profit forecast to 49 billion yen ($437 million) from a 51 billion yen ($455 million) forecast made in late May, although the latest estimate was still higher than actual profit of 45.3 billion yen ($404 million) a year earlier.
It maintained its prediction of 1.77 trillion yen ($15.8 billion) for group sales for the full year.
Net profit is obtained by subtracting extraordinary profit or losses from current earnings and then deducting taxes.

The yen's comparative weakness from year-ago levels also helped to support Sharp's half-year group earnings, but the benefits of the weak yen appear to have declined as the company has boosted production abroad.
"The yen's weakness is one positive factor, but the effect of a weaker yen is getting smaller than in the past due to increased overseas output," the official said. ($1=112 yen)
